analysis.title: GS Garrett - weekend prep 25 Oct 2026
key_insights: Desk conversations are at peak frustration as YTD P&L ratchets lower with fewer sessions left. Net exposure fell about a month ago and remains at the 0th percentile. Gross exposure fell this week, the largest weekly de-gross since July.

Breadth improved (two-thirds of SPX names were green on the week) and the index fell only 50bps wire to wire, but the damage underneath was large. Fundamental L/S drew down another 1.1% and systematics had their worst week since 2024.
Index options now reflect an expected loud macro and micro tape this week: NDX 1-week straddle at 3% (about 1-year high) and SPX 1-week straddle at 1.8% (about 60th percentile).

The GS momentum factor basket (GSPRHIMO) has had 30 daily moves of +/-5% in 2026, more than any other year in the dataset (2000, 2009, 2020 included) with two months left. The desk cites this as evidence of trader exhaustion.

Garrett frames two scenarios: the 2nd inning of a repricing of the whole AI ecosystem (index has material downside catch-down) or the 8th inning of a significant de-gross episode. He leans toward the de-gross camp.
For the de-gross view to play out, Garrett wants bond volatility to subside, the midterms out of the way, proof of AI capex payback in earnings, and oil below 90.

US equities were net sold for the third straight week (four of the last five). Single stocks saw the largest de-gross since late July. Global net selling was driven entirely by long selling, into a week where 44% of SPX companies report EPS.
Cash desk saw risk-off flows led by TMT, with long-only and hedge fund clients both better sellers. TMT selling totals $20bn over two weeks, approaching July's AI unwind at -$23bn.

Equity CTAs are long $48bn of global stocks, almost all US, and are already short most global indices. They sit on top of the medium-term thresholds in both SPX and NDX, below which additional selling is triggered.

Bond CTAs have been massively short fixed income for months. The retrace lower in global yields (5.02% in US10Y was key) created a technical demand tailwind. They are short $300bn in total at current levels (short $145mm DV01).
Bond CTA cover estimates: a flat tape over 1 week means covering $12bn DV01 (+$25bn in an up tape). A flat tape over 1 month means covering $42bn DV01 (+$165bn in an up tape).

Volatility compressed slightly after last Friday's panic bid (delta-adjusted VIX hit about 1-year highs), but scar tissue remains. The VIX market is more nervous than the SPX market over the next month: VIX call vol is at an extreme while SPX put vol is mid-percentile.
Cash and derivative volumes dried up into the weekend, consistent with lower gross exposure.

The Brazilian election result is due within hours of the note. The vol surface prices an asymmetric -22% / +13% two-way outcome, in contrast to zero excess variance priced in SPX and QQQ for the US midterms.
AAPL is negatively correlated to the NDX for the first time in history.

The AI winners vs AI at risk pair is down 13% YTD. SPXXAI has outperformed SPX by 7.4% over the last 3 weeks. The desk says short-term stops outweigh medium-term fundamentals and likes upside call spreads in the AI basket.

sector_views.rationale: Heavy TMT selling ($20bn over two weeks) and the AI ecosystem repricing debate, but the desk likes upside call spreads in the AI basket as a de-gross episode trade.

earnings_insights: 44% of SPX companies report EPS in the week following the note, described as one of the most consequential earnings weeks of the year.
Garrett says proof of AI capex payback in earnings is one condition needed for the de-gross episode to end.

macro_indicators.interpretation: 5.02% was a key level. The retrace lower in yields created a technical demand tailwind as bond CTAs hold a large short.
Garrett says oil below 90 would help the de-gross episode resolve.

trade_ideas.rationale: The desk says we are in the middle of a de-gross episode where short-term stops outweigh medium-term fundamentals.

risk_factors: Further de-grossing and long selling into a heavy earnings week.
Bond volatility staying elevated, with yields near 5% on the US10Y.
Insufficient proof of AI capex payback in earnings.
Equity CTA selling if SPX and NDX break the medium-term thresholds.
A broader repricing of the AI ecosystem.
vol_and_positioning: NDX 1-week straddle at 3% (about 1-year highs). SPX 1-week straddle at 1.8% (about 60th percentile).
Delta-adjusted VIX hit about 1-year highs last Friday. VIX call vol is extreme while SPX put vol is mid-percentile.
Net exposure remains at the 0th percentile. Gross had its largest weekly de-gross since July.
Equity CTAs are long $48bn of global stocks and sit on the medium-term thresholds in SPX and NDX.
Bond CTAs are short $300bn total (short $145mm DV01). Cover estimates: $12bn DV01 over 1 week on a flat tape and $42bn over 1 month.
Fundamental L/S: -1.1% on the week, -3.8% MTD, +8.8% YTD (after a +17.4% high-water mark in June quarter). Systematic L/S: -2% on the week, -1.1% MTD, +18.7% YTD.
GS momentum factor basket has had 30 moves of +/-5% YTD, versus 23 in 2000 (avg VIX 23), 16 in 2009 (avg VIX 31) and 21 in 2020 (avg VIX 29).
geopolitical: Brazilian presidential election results expected within hours of the note, with the vol surface pricing an asymmetric two-way move.
US midterm elections are named as a needed hurdle to clear, with no excess variance priced in SPX or QQQ.
